questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to have the be able to speak the language and also develop better English skills. It was quite important to go to a country with opportunities of trying out interesting courses suitable for my degree.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since Copenhagen University provided me with a information sheet.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a sheet with links to information about the available universities and the need of qualifications to apply for the universities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of the information was quite unorganized and confusing most of the time. But we had an orientation day which helped me to understand most of the information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Rooms with or without bathroom. And an option of having roommates.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Both but you needed a kitchen to cook. And since I did not have a kitchen I needed to have a meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I can recommend to have a kitchen rather than having the meal plan. If you take the meal plan then the bronze meal plan is more than enough to satisfy the food need.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy to access the different possibilities of courses. To registry for the courses I needed to mail the head of the apartment to be registered. But I was pretty easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Different links on their websites. Additionally, the student services were quick to respond to my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For any questions ask the Student Services. Otherwise the registration was easy and understandable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was said that the courses at 4000-levels were difficult. Therefore I only took 2000- and 3000-level courses. They were suitable for my third year of university level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was mostly long lectures with no or small breaks. Additionally, a lot of writing and tests were needed to be handed in every week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1010 Design, 2010 Social Determinants of Health, 2020 Politics of Health Policy Analysis and 3170 Health Psychology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
2010 Social Determinants of Health: the professor is nice and the course is very interesting. Additionally, the assignments during the course is doable. 
3170 Health Psychology: A course that was very good with a lot of course material which you will have test in during every week. However, this is a great way for you to understand and remember the course material.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really. I had expected the costs of the transportation and personal spending.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food on the restaurants were less expensive than I have expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Tait MacKenzie Center was nice with their options to exercise.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot different ones. They often had games for the different sports at the university and events posted on their walls of different options. Their Instagram account is also good.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports events since the events have a great atmosphere.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go Downtown in Toronto. The Algonquin Provincial Park is also great to go visit during a holiday as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Although the food options were not super healthy and different from the Danish food styles.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food options since I missed some more fresh food and great bread. But otherwise the cultural was easy to adapt to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The chill vibes in Kensington Market are real cool and nice plus the Spadina area.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go out and explore Downtown during the weekends. 
2) Socialize early and establish friendships with the other exchange students.
3) Be sure to keep yourself updated and follow along the courses from the beginning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend the lectures and handin the assignments (both small and big ones).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To establish International friendships and experience Canada.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To keep updated with the reading material in all courses in some periods of the semester. But the exam period was more relaxed hereby.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is fun to go on exchange. I recommend to do it for everyone!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
